text:
Here is the test suite in Gherkin (BDD DSL) notation:

```gherkin
Feature: Doorstop Requirements Management

  Scenario: Store requirements in a permanent and secure manner
    Given a new requirement is added to Doorstop
    When the requirement is saved
    Then the requirement is stored in a permanent and secure manner

  Scenario: Handle change management of the requirements
    Given a requirement is modified in Doorstop
    When the change is saved
    Then the change is tracked and associated with the developer who made the change

  Scenario: Associate requirements changes to existing developer identification
    Given a developer is assigned to a requirement in Doorstop
    When the requirement is modified
    Then the change is associated with the developer's identification

  Scenario: Be scalable to support thousands of requirements
    Given Doorstop has 1000 requirements
    When a new requirement is added
    Then the system does not crash and the requirement is stored correctly

  Scenario: Provide a lightweight installation method
    Given Doorstop is installed on a new system
    When the installation is complete
    Then the system is up and running with minimal configuration required

  Scenario Outline: Store requirements in a permanent and secure manner with different data types
    Given a new requirement with <data_type> data is added to Doorstop
    When the requirement is saved
    Then the requirement is stored in a permanent and secure manner
    Examples:
      | data_type    |
      | string       |
      | integer      |
      | float        |
      | boolean      |
      | date         |
      | time         |
      | datetime     |

  Scenario Outline: Handle change management of the requirements with different change types
    Given a requirement is modified with <change_type> in Doorstop
    When the change is saved
    Then the change is tracked and associated with the developer who made the change
    Examples:
      | change_type    |
      | minor change   |
      | major change   |
      | deletion       |
      | addition       |

  Scenario Outline: Associate requirements changes to existing developer identification with different developer roles
    Given a developer with <developer_role> is assigned to a requirement in Doorstop
    When the requirement is modified
    Then the change is associated with the developer's identification
    Examples:
      | developer_role    |
      | developer         |
      | administrator     |
      | guest             |
```

And here is the JSON list of test cases:

```json
[
  {"id": "TC-001", "title": "Store requirements in a permanent and secure manner", "req_ids": ["REQ011"], "kind": "positive", "preconditions": ["new requirement is added"], "inputs": {"requirement": "example requirement"}, "steps": ["requirement is saved", "requirement is stored in a permanent and secure manner"], "expected": ["requirement is stored correctly"]},
  {"id": "TC-002", "title": "Handle change management of the requirements", "req_ids": ["REQ012"], "kind": "positive", "preconditions": ["requirement is modified"], "inputs": {"change": "example change"}, "steps": ["change is saved", "change is tracked and associated with developer"], "expected": ["change is tracked correctly"]},
  {"id": "TC-003", "title": "Associate requirements changes to existing developer identification", "req_ids": ["REQ013"], "kind": "positive", "preconditions": ["developer is assigned to requirement"], "inputs": {"developer": "example developer"}, "steps": ["requirement is modified", "change is associated with developer's identification"], "expected": ["change is associated correctly"]},
  {"id": "TC-004", "title": "Be scalable to support thousands of requirements", "req_ids": ["REQ014"], "kind": "positive", "preconditions": ["Doorstop has 1000 requirements"], "inputs": {"new requirement": "example requirement"}, "steps": ["new requirement is added", "system does not crash"], "expected": ["requirement is stored correctly"]},
  {"id": "TC-005", "title": "Provide a lightweight installation method", "req_ids": ["REQ015"], "kind": "positive", "preconditions": ["Doorstop is installed on new system"], "inputs": {"installation": "example installation"}, "steps": ["installation is complete", "system is up and running"], "expected": ["system is up and running correctly"]},
  {"id": "TC-006", "title": "Store requirements in a permanent and secure manner with different data types", "req_ids": ["REQ011"], "kind": "positive", "preconditions": ["new requirement with data type is added"], "inputs": {"data_type": "string"}, "steps": ["requirement is saved", "requirement is stored in a permanent and secure manner"], "expected": ["requirement is stored correctly"]},
  {"id": "TC-007", "title": "Handle change management of the requirements with different change types", "req_ids": ["REQ012"], "kind": "positive", "preconditions": ["requirement is modified with change type"], "inputs": {"change_type": "minor change"}, "steps": ["change is saved", "change is tracked and associated with developer"], "expected": ["change is tracked correctly"]},
  {"id": "TC-008", "title": "Associate requirements changes to existing developer identification with different developer roles", "req_ids": ["REQ013"], "kind": "positive", "preconditions": ["developer with role is assigned to requirement"], "inputs": {"developer_role": "developer"}, "steps": ["requirement is modified", "change is associated with developer's identification"], "expected": ["change is associated correctly"]}
]
```
